discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS experiments at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize honoured the prediction of the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism; the experimental achievement that confirmed it remains unrecognised. Peter Jenni (founding ATLAS spokesperson), Michel Della Negra and Tejinder Virdee (founders of CMS) conceived these general-purpose detectors in the late 1980s and early 1990s. They set the design principles, notably precision electromagnetic calorimetry and muon spectrometry optimised for H to gamma-gamma and H to four leptons, and led them through two decades of construction. In July 2012 both experiments independently observed a new scalar boson near 125 GeV, establishing the first elementary spin-zero particle. Its measured couplings now test the Standard Model's least understood sector, and its mass places the electroweak vacuum near criticality. These findings frame today's central questions about naturalness and physics beyond the Standard Model. Their leadership made this discovery possible.
